preamble: Vocalization of word-final /s/ to the palatal glide [j] happened in Italian and Romanian, mostly in monosyllables, where Latin nōs, vōs, post and trēs end in a falling diphthong (Italian noi, poi; Romanian noi, trei). Italian also preserves the alternative outcome, in which the final sibilant was lost or assimilated (tre < trēs, ma < magis beside mai). This is a regionally restricted Romance development, not a widespread cross-linguistic shift.

examples.note: The final sibilant of the monosyllable was vocalized to a palatal off-glide.
Same vocalization of final -s; compare Latin magis > mai beside ma.
Romanian has the glide where Italian tre lost the final sibilant.
Gravina lists *s → j as a regular Malgbe change, earlier than Malgbe *ts → s, which therefore did not merge with j.

sources: Università degli Studi di Cagliari (2020). Linguistica italiana 2: etimi di pioppo, ma, io (course notes). https://web.unica.it/static/resources/cms/documents/Linguistica2.Etimipioppoma.Chiusuravocaliiniato.pdf
